newsitem.title: USA: U.S. adj retail sales up 2.5 pct in Feb - Redbook.
newsitem.headline: U.S. adj retail sales up 2.5 pct in Feb - Redbook.

text.p: U.S. seasonally adjusted retail sales rose 2.5 percent in the first three weeks of fiscal February versus January, according to the Lynch, Jones & Ryan Inc Redbook Retail Sales Index.

The index rose 5.8 percent compared to the same month a year ago, the report said. Adjusted retail sales advanced 5.1 percent in the week ended February 22 compared with the same week a year ago, it said.
Soft-line merchandise continued to dominate at both national and regional department stores, said Howard Eilenberg, a retail analyst at Redbook Research.
"We hear good remarks from the department stores that their better-apparel business is doing well," said Eilenberg in an interview with Reuters Financial Television.
Eilenberg said discount sales were mostly driven by electronics, toys and consumables. But apparel sales is "below the average," resulting in a mixed bag of results, he said.

The Presidents' Day holiday weekend last week offered retailers additional opportunities to clear remaining fall and winter inventories, but sales tapered off toward the end of the week, Eilenberg said.
"The first two weeks in (February) were very good, but the third week that just past was a little slower," he said, adding that "there is still some merchandise on hand."
While last week's retail sales may not have been astounding, February sales seem to be on target.
"It's not upsetting anybody when you see figures like that," Eilenberg added.
